G-optimality (GOPTPEV)

Source: vignettes/articles/criterion-gopt.Rmd
criterion-gopt.Rmd

G-optimality minimizes the largest eigenvalue of the PEV matrix of the target, the variance in the worst direction.

Type Optimal design
Direction Smaller is better
Uses a test set yes
Score a given set gopt_score()
Search with it optTrain(method = "GOpt")

Definition

With BB as for PEVmax: G=λmax(X0BX0′)\mathrm{G} = \lambda_{\max}(X_0 B X_0'), computed from the p×pp \times p matrix L−1X0′X0L−TL^{-1}X_0'X_0L^{-T} with LL′=X′X+λILL' = X'X + \lambda I.

Use in TSDFGS 

library(TSDFGS)
data(geno)
gopt_score(geno[1:50, ], geno[51:100, ])
## [1] 20127415
fit <- optTrain(geno, cand = 1:404, n.train = 50, method = "GOpt",
                 min.iter = 300, console = FALSE, seed = 1)
fit$OPTtrain
##  [1] 391 347 173 336 127 315 146  62 342 393 330 290 134 153 158 369 297 217 392
## [20] 389 390 128 373 244 350 364 222 162  69 304  20 283 343 300 151 376  81  15
## [39] 229  44 135 298 149 160  36 388  45 250 281  80
# targeted: the test set is known
fit2 <- optTrain(geno, cand = 1:300, n.train = 50, test = 301:404,
                  method = "GOpt", min.iter = 300, console = FALSE, seed = 1)
fit2$OPTtrain
##  [1] 256 126 143 137 140  93  97  84 298 129 196 278  31  89 259 152 127  44 168
## [20]  76 108 212  71 117 198 216 162 232  67  39 245  74  10 220  72  24 300  52
## [39] 151 150  65 225 260  32 141 116 230 249  43  77

The search is a random-start exchange (hill-climbing) search; see How the scores are computed. Use min.iter larger than 300 on real data and check fit$converged.

Original work

Akdemir, D., Sanchez, J. I., & Jannink, J.-L. (2015). Optimization of genomic selection training populations with a genetic algorithm. Genetics Selection Evolution, 47, 38. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12711-015-0116-6

Isidro y Sánchez, J., & Akdemir, D. (2021). Training set optimization for sparse phenotyping in genomic selection: a conceptual overview. Frontiers in Plant Science, 12, 715910. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpls.2021.715910

Repository or website of the original authors: R package STPGA by Akdemir and colleagues: CRAN.R-project.org/package=STPGA (GPL-3).

License review

This is our reading of the public record, not legal advice; see the license review.
